priorInvolvementDisclosure: I authored the frozen Claude v35 REJECT, whose blocker was that kexecCapability was a constant with no derivation and no signed carriage. v36 applies both remedies I named, which is the situation most at risk of a confirmatory read. whyThisIsAccept.theChainVerified: The proof now closes end to end, and each link is a stated operation rather than an assertion. First, the member is pinned: authenticatedKernelMember requires relativePath to select exactly one regular-file authenticatedManifest member, with zero or multiple matches refusing, and sha256 to equal that same member's sha256. Second, those bytes are tied to what actually ran: peCoffImageDigest MUST be recomputed from those same exact member bytes by peCoffImageDigestAlgorithm and MUST equal both the retained field and kernelEvent.digestSha256, and kernelEvent is the transcript-authenticated PCR-4 application immediately following the boot-manager action for BootCurrent. Third, kexec absence is derived from those same bytes: kexecAbsenceDerivation takes as input 'the exact authenticatedManifest member bytes selected by authenticatedKernelMember.relativePath (the same bytes used for sha256 and peCoffImageDigest)', locates the IKCONFIG blob, and requires CONFIG_KEXEC, CONFIG_KEXEC_FILE, CONFIG_KEXEC_CORE, CONFIG_CRASH_DUMP and CONFIG_KEXEC_JUMP each absent or n, with y or m refusing. Fourth, a signer attests it: signedObject.kexecCapability is required on Linux, must equal the derivation output for this entry's member bytes, is keyed to the same platformProfileKey and OS-ABI entry as measuredBootTranscriptDigest, and refuses cross-entry substitution. Taken together: the bytes that were launched contain no kexec entry point, so no replacement can occur, so the kernel answering any later question is the launched kernel. That is a structural proof rather than a self-report, and it is the first version of this bind that does not rest on asking the kernel about itself.
whyThisIsAccept.theOverclaimCorrected: The v35 role sentence that claimed independence from self-reports while depending on one is gone. presentState now reads 'CORROBORATION only ... Present-state absence is not the structural proof', role reads 'kexec-absent is a fact about authenticated member bytes plus a signed inventory attestation. Present-state procfs only corroborates', NT-TCB-KEXEC keys its refusals on the derivation and marks the procfs clause '(corroboration)', and g22.doesNotClaim states it 'does not treat procfs as the structural proof'. kexecAbsenceDerivation.notThis names the v35 defect in its own words: 'a constant token, a procfs self-report, or OptionalData tokens.'
whyThisIsAccept.failureSemanticsFailClosed: Derivation failure is not silent. 'Truncation, bad gzip, or missing markers after both searches refuses', so a kernel built without IKCONFIG refuses rather than defaulting to the safe-looking answer, and refusesBootConfigs and unavailableRefuses both enumerate the new failure modes — missing IKCONFIG, any requiredN symbol y or m, signed kexecCapability mismatch, malformed FilePathList parse. The resulting narrowing of the qualifying population is stated in inScopeBootConfigs, which is the propagation this contract missed at v33 and v34 and gets right here.
whyThisIsAccept.attacksThatFailed: I could not construct a machine that passes while a replacement has occurred. The v35 attack — launch a kexec-capable kernel, use its kexec path, present a kernel that hides the sysctl — now fails at the derivation, because the sysctl is no longer what is examined: the launched image's own embedded configuration is, and it is bound to kernelEvent by digest. Substituting the analysed bytes would require breaking the peCoffImageDigest equality to the measured event. Spoofing the IKCONFIG blob would require altering the authenticated member, which changes its sha256 and its Authenticode digest. Skipping the derivation fails closed at both refusal enumerations.

codexSubRequirementConsidered.item: PTCB-V35-B2 asked for the capability evidence object to be defined 'with observer namespace and failure semantics fixed.'
codexSubRequirementConsidered.status: Failure semantics are fixed; observer namespace is not stated for the procfs corroboration reads. observerNamespace occurs zero times, and the existing mountNamespaceIdentity machinery is not tied to these reads.
codexSubRequirementConsidered.whyNotFiled: I considered filing this and concluded it is not a defect in this generation. The namespace question mattered while procfs carried the proof; it no longer does. The structural proof is the derivation over authenticated bytes, which involves no procfs and no namespace. An unfixed namespace can only weaken the corroboration in the passing direction — a masked or absent /proc yields absence, which merely fails to add corroboration to a fact already established — or refuse in the failing direction, which is fail-closed. Neither outcome can admit a machine whose executing kernel differs from the launched one, and neither produces a determinable divergence in the verdict, because the derivation governs. Filing it would be holding a corroboration-only check to a standard that only the load-bearing check needs to meet. I record the judgement here so that a coordinator or a later reviewer who disagrees can see it was considered rather than overlooked, and can require the namespace to be pinned as a hardening item without reopening this verdict.

repairsVerified.finding: CLAUDE-V35-B1 (mine) — kexecCapability was a constant with no derivation, no signed carriage, and a procfs read as the only operative evidence
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED by both routes I named. Route one: kexecAbsenceDerivation is a named operation over the authenticated member's exact bytes, with a two-step search — direct IKCFG_ST/IKCFG_ED marker scan, falling back to a bzImage payload parse that reads setup_header payload_offset and payload_length and decompresses by magic for gzip, xz, zstd or lz4 — then gunzip of the blob to .config text and a closed five-symbol absence rule. The two-step search also covers both slice-1 Linux architectures, since an arm64 EFI-stub Image is uncompressed and resolves at step one while an x86_64 bzImage carries its configuration inside the compressed payload and resolves at step two. Route two: signedObject.kexecCapability is required on Linux, forbidden on macOS, must equal the derivation output for this entry's member bytes, and refuses cross-entry substitution. The closed shapes were updated to match rather than left contradicting the addition — linuxForm is 'exactly {tag, pathlessObservation, measuredBootTranscriptDigest, kexecCapability}' with extras rejected, macosForm 'exactly {tag, pathlessObservation}' — which is the propagation failure I have filed against this contract three times and which does not occur here.

limitsOfThisReview: I reviewed the four predecessor findings, the new derivation and its signed carriage, the restored joins and load-option parse, the closed change roster, the pin chain, the live register/COORD/file-04 carries and the authority refusals. Paths outside this round's roster were checked only for unchangedness, and the roster is accurate this round. My assessment of the derivation rests on the documented behaviour of the interfaces it names — the IKCONFIG marker format and gzip blob, the x86 bzImage setup-header payload fields, and the kernel configuration symbols that gate each replacement entry point — not on execution against a live machine or against a specific kernel build. summary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Custody is clean throughout: the subject is unmoved at 9d4779b6... and mode 0444 at start and end, HEAD never left 93ceaa6, all 53 chain pins reproduce, both frozen v35 verdicts reproduce with no replacement, the v35-to-v36 diff is 36 paths with zero off-roster, reviewGuidance is a pure prefix-preserving append, the sole DR-126 row is quoted byte-exactly, all three remeasurement pins reproduce, and all 33 D-096 occurrences are refusals. Every predecessor finding is repaired. Codex's joins are restored with each MUST it enumerated. Its load-option parse is restored for FilePathList alone while OptionalData stays opaque and non-security-bearing. And the blocker that Codex and I reached independently is closed by both of the routes I named rather than one. kexecAbsenceDerivation is a real operation over the exact authenticated member bytes: it locates the embedded kernel configuration, by direct marker scan or by parsing and decompressing the bzImage payload, and requires every kexec entry point — the two syscalls, the core umbrella, crash-dump kexec and kexec jump — to be absent or n, refusing on y or m and refusing when the configuration cannot be found at all. Those same bytes carry the Authenticode digest that must equal the transcript-authenticated kernelEvent, so what is analysed is what was launched; and the derived token is additionally attested on the Linux PATHLESS signedObject, keyed to the same entry as the transcript digest with cross-entry substitution refused, with both closed platform shapes updated so the new field does not contradict the schema that carries it. The v35 overclaim is retracted in four places and procfs is corroboration only. I could not construct a machine that passes while a replacement has occurred: the attack that defeated v35 now fails at the derivation, and defeating the derivation would require altering bytes whose digest is pinned to the measured launch. The stale-reference sweep that produced findings against five earlier generations returns clean, the closed roster is accurate, and every new condition reaches the scope and refusal enumerations. One sub-clause of Codex's required repair, fixing the observer namespace for the procfs reads, is not literally present; I record in codexSubRequirementConsidered why that is not a defect now that procfs cannot carry the proof, so the judgement is visible rather than silent and can be revisited as hardening without disturbing this verdict. ACCEPT is a verdict on this candidate only: DR-126 stays OPEN, the artifact stays CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and DO-NOT-SEAL, G22 stays NAMED-NOT-QUALIFIED, and nothing here authorizes docs/v2/implementation/ or mints a D-096 (A) grant.
